title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: Advanced review set explorer for KQL queries
summary: The briefing passes: its access controls, audit-search instructions, licensing qualifications and documented limits are supported. It correctly distinguishes the roadmap's targets and cloud listing from Microsoft's tenant notice, and identifies the explorer as preview.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The Advanced Review Set Explorer is a new experience in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium) review sets.
claims.quote: We’re introducing the Advanced Review Set Explorer (public preview) for review sets in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium).

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The explorer provides a Kusto Query Language query tab in review sets.
claims.quote:
Select a review set, and then select the **Advanced review set explorer (preview)** tab.

From here, you can write and run KQL queries directly against the review set data.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Reviewers can use complex filters on review set data.
claims.quote: Build powerful queries with complex filtering, pattern-based text extraction, and data format parsing.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Reviewers can aggregate review set data with KQL.
claims.quote: The `summarize` operator aggregates data by applying functions like `count()`, `sum()`, or `avg()`, and groups results based on specified columns.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The explorer supports pattern-based text extraction from review set items.
claims.quote: Build powerful queries with complex filtering, pattern-based text extraction, and data format parsing.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Query results can be displayed as a table or chart.
claims.quote: Queries run against the full set of indexed items and return either tabular results or chart visualizations.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Existing KeyQL-based review set searching remains supported without change alongside KQL.
claims.quote: Users can continue using existing KeyQL‑based searching within review set without change.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The notice says no existing queries or workflows are modified.
claims.quote: No existing queries or workflows are modified.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; front matter: changes
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn currently documents the explorer as preview.
claims.quote: Search content in a review set with the Advanced review set explorer (preview)

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The explorer opens at Microsoft Purview portal > eDiscovery > Cases > case > Review sets > review set > Advanced review set explorer (preview).
claims.quote:
Select the **eDiscovery** solution card, and then select **Cases** in the left navigation.
3. Select a case, and then select the **Review sets** tab.
4. Select a review set, and then select the **Advanced review set explorer (preview)** tab.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Explorer queries run against the current review set's indexed items rather than a new data source.
claims.quote: All queries in the Advanced review set explorer (preview) run against the current review set’s indexed items. You don't need to specify a table name. The review set acts as the default data source.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure, Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Queries are read-only and do not modify review set content.
claims.quote: Queries are read-only and don't modify review set content.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Queries returning more than 10,000 results return only the first 10,000.
claims.quote: If the query returns more than 10,000 results, it returns only the first 10,000 results. Modify the query to narrow down the results.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The explorer does not support every Kusto operator or property.
claims.quote: The Advanced review set explorer (preview) doesn't support all Kusto operators and properties.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Older review sets may lack KQL properties and return column-not-found errors for those properties.
claims.quote: Some older review sets might not support certain KQL properties if those properties weren't available when the review set was created and data was generated. Querying an unsupported property in an older review set results in a column not found error.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn recommends creating a new review set with Add to review set to regenerate data with supported properties.
claims.quote: To resolve this error, create a new review set and use the **Add to review set** process to regenerate the data with the latest supported properties.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Learn lists common KQL syntax errors and their fixes.
claims.quote:
When you create queries in the Advanced review set explorer (preview), you might encounter syntax errors.

The following table lists common errors and how to fix them:

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Learn includes an example listing external recipient email addresses for each review set item.
claims.quote: Find all review set items that include at least one external recipient (outside your organization contoso.com), and list those external email addresses for each item.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Adding data to the review set can change the results of a later query.
claims.quote: Results reflect the current indexed state of the review set. If you add more data to the review set, the query might return different results.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The Review role permits access to review sets in cases of which the user is a member.
claims.quote: This role lets users access review sets in eDiscovery. Users who are assigned this role can see and open the list of cases that they're members of.

claims.where: Scope; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The eDiscovery Manager and Administrator groups and the Reviewer group hold the Review role by default.
claims.quote:
| Role | Compliance Administrator | eDiscovery Manager & Administrator | Organization Management | Reviewer |
| Review |  | ![Check mark indicating the Review role is assigned to eDiscovery Manager and Administrator.](media/checkmark.png) |  | ![Check mark](media/checkmark.png) |

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: Role membership is managed at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Role groups > eDiscovery Manager > Edit > Manage eDiscovery Manager > Choose users or Choose groups.
claims.quote:
Go to **Settings** > **Role groups**.
3. On **Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions**, select **eDiscovery Manager**.
Select **Edit**.
On **Manage eDiscovery Manager**, select **Choose users** or **Choose groups**.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls
claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group> adds the specified group to the eDiscovery Managers subgroup.
claims.quote: You can add a mail-enabled security group as a member of the eDiscovery Managers subgroup in the *eDiscovery Manager* role group by using the **Add-RoleGroupMember** cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The group supplied to this Add-RoleGroupMember example must be mail-enabled security rather than a distribution or Microsoft 365 group.
claims.quote: Exchange distribution groups and Microsoft 365 Groups aren't supported. You must use a mail-enabled security group

The audit log records eDiscovery activities that you perform in Microsoft Purview portal or in PowerShell.
Creating eDiscovery review sets and performing review activities in cases.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Searching the audit log requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the *Audit Logs* or *View-Only Audit Logs* roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Accessing audit cmdlets requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs in the Exchange admin center.
claims.quote: To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the *Audit Logs* or *View-Only Audit Logs* roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: Analysing a user's data with premium eDiscovery features requires that user to have Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5, subject to the stated add-on alternative.
claims.quote: To analyze a user's data when premium eDiscovery features are enabled, the user must be assigned an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: Users with Office 365 E1, Office 365 E3 or Microsoft 365 E3 can instead receive Microsoft Purview Suite or the Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on.
claims.quote: Alternatively, users with an Office 365 E1 or an Office 365 or Microsoft 365 E3 license can be assigned a Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Administrators, compliance officers and legal personnel assigned as case members do not need E5 to collect, view and analyse data with premium features.
claims.quote: Administrators, compliance officers, or legal personnel who are assigned to cases as members and use premium eDiscovery features to collect, view, and analyze data don't need an E5 license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost

claims.quote: To analyze a user's data when premium eDiscovery features are enabled, the user must be assigned an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Learn's explorer instructions require signing in with an account assigned eDiscovery permissions.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: The KQL experience is intended to give advanced reviewers greater flexibility to slice, aggregate and analyse review set data than their existing query experience.
claims.quote: power users and advanced reviewers often need greater flexibility to slice, aggregate, and analyze review set data in more sophisticated ways. To meet this need, we’re adding a Kusto Query Language (KQL)–based experience
